'''Trevor John McMillan''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|OBE|FRCR|FRSB}} (born 2 October 1959) is an English [[radiobiologist]] who was Vice-Chancellor of [[Keele University]] from 10 August 2015 to September 2025 .<ref>Keele University VC [https://www.keele.ac.uk/vco/vice-chancellor/]. Retrieved on 13 January 2016.</ref><ref>Media release on appointment as VC at Keele [https://www.keele.ac.uk/pressreleases/2015/keeleannouncesappointmentofnextvice-chancellor.html]. 13 March 2015. Retrieved on 13 January 2016</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-28 |title=Vice-Chancellor Trevor McMillan OBE retires after a decade at Keele |url=https://www.keele.ac.uk/about/news/2025/august/trevor-mcmillan/vice-chancellor-retirement.php |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Keele University |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Born in [[Gateshead]], McMillan was educated at Birtley Lord Lawson Comprehensive School, UK before studying Biological Sciences at [[Lancaster University]], graduating in 1981. He was awarded a PhD in Biophysics at the [[Institute of Cancer Research]], [[University of London]] in 1984.

==Career==
McMillan's early research was carried out at the [[Institute of Cancer Research]]/[[Royal Marsden Hospital]] and the [[Imperial Cancer Research Fund]]. McMillan has published widely on the use of X-rays in [[radiotherapy]] and the harmful effects of long wavelength UV radiation in sunlight. In particular his research has examined the role of DNA damage and repair in the efficacy of radiotherapy and the harmful cellular effects of UVA following environmentally relevant exposures.<ref>Review summarising research on UVA [http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1211/jpp.60.8.0004/epdf]. [[Journal of Pharmacy and Pharmacology]]. March 31, 2008. Retrieved 13 January 2016</ref>

Before moving to Keele as Deputy Vice-Chancellor and Provost in January 2014, he was at [[Lancaster University]] where he had several roles including Dean of the Institute of Environmental and Natural Sciences, Head of the Department of Biological Sciences and finally Pro Vice-Chancellor for Research (2005–2014). During this time he chaired the Research and Enterprise Committee for the [[1994 Group]] of Universities in which he led the publication of “Enterprising Universities - Using the Research Base to add Value to Business”. He also Chaired the Management Committee of the [[N8 Research Partnership]].<ref>N8 research collaboration [http://www.n8research.org.uk/universities-and-science-minister-to-launch-research-collaboration/]. 15 September 2011. Retrieved 13 January 2016</ref>

==Professional activities==
On the basis of his research, McMillan has worked on national committees that have examined the harmful effects of radiation in the environment. These included [[COMARE]] (Committee on Medical Aspects of Radiation in the Environment)<ref>COMARE - Committee on Medical Aspects of Radiation in the Environment [https://www.gov.uk/government/groups/committee-on-medical-aspects-of-radiation-in-the-environment-comare]. Retrieved 13 January 2016</ref> for the [[Department of Health]].

He is currently on the Advisory Group for Ionising Radiation<ref>Advisory Group for Ionising Radiation [https://www.gov.uk/government/groups/advisory-group-on-ionising-radiation-agir]. Retrieved 13 January 2016</ref> for [[Public Health England]] and the Advisory Group for the [[National Institute for Health Research]] (NIHR) Health Protection Research Unit (HPRU) in Chemical and Radiation Threats and Hazards at [[Newcastle University]]. He led the production of the report Circulatory Disease Risk for the AGIR.<ref>Circulatory Disease Risk [https://www.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/334374/RCE-16_for_web.pdf]. October, 2010. Retrieved 13 January 2016</ref> He has recently (December 2015) been announced as the Knowledge Exchange Framework champion for [[Higher Education Funding Council for England]] (HEFCE).<ref>Doing better knowledge exchange [http://blog.hefce.ac.uk/2015/12/15/doing-better-knowledge-exchange/]. 15 December 2015. Retrieved 13 January 2016</ref>

==Honours and awards==
McMillan has been awarded Honorary Fellowship of the [[Royal College of Radiologists]] and Honorary Membership of the [[Royal College of Physicians]]. He is also a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Biology]].

He was appointed [[Officer of the Order of the British Empire]] (OBE) in the [[2022 Birthday Honours]] for services to higher education.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63714|supp=y|page=B14|date=1 June 2022}}</ref>
